summary_check.issues: Conflates cash and credit-ledger uses: credit pays output tax only, not interest, penalty or fees; also omits the statutory credit-use cap power.
summary_check.corrected_summary: Cash deposits and self-assessed eligible credit enter separate electronic ledgers: cash may discharge prescribed dues, while credit is restricted to output tax subject to utilisation and cross-tax restrictions and prescribed limits. The section governs refunds, liability recording and payment priority, presumes tax incidence is passed on unless proved otherwise, and permits specified cash-ledger transfers including to distinct persons subject to unpaid-liability restrictions. Government may prescribe a maximum proportion of output tax payable through credit, and the explanation defines deposit date and tax versus other dues.

metadata_check.issues: Credit-ledger funds cannot pay interest, penalties, fees or other non-output-tax amounts. Distinct-person transfers concern cash and specified tax heads, not arbitrary credit transfers; omitted subsection (12), cross-CGST/SGST prohibitions and rebuttable incidence presumption.
